summary: NDJSON ordered export: tenant-case-preserving IDs, HEC handshake/resume-token mismatch, and RFC3161-signed manifest request
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (FinTrak Bank) reports discrepancies in the NDJSON SIEM export for tenant-scoped activity. The customer has strict regulatory requirements that event ordering must be preserved and tenant identifiers must be case-preserving (not lowercased) for downstream reconciliation with their PSP. They also require an RFC3161 timestamped manifest and evidence that the export manifest was signed by our KMS and anchored with an HSM-backed key.

Impact:
- Missing/duplicated events reported during daily reconciliation leading to finance and compliance variance reports.
- Tenant ID case normalization causes mismatches in customer processing pipelines (FinTrak's join is case-sensitive).
- Customer cannot accept exported bundles without RFC3161-signed manifest for chain-of-custody.

Environment:
- Production exports via S3 NDJSON delivery (audit-log-stream-v2), account region: us-east-1.
- HEC-forwarding to customer-managed Splunk via HEC (customer uses a shared inlet expecting idempotent resume tokens).

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Query export endpoint for tenant "FinTrak\u003aLoginCorp" for time window 2026-03-08T00:00:00Z to 2026-03-09T00:00:00Z.
   curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <cust-token>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/export?tenant=FinTrak%3ALoginCorp&from=2026-03-08T00:00:00Z&to=2026-03-09T00:00:00Z&format=ndjson"
2) Download manifest and payload from S3 bucket: s3://redwood-exports/fintrak/2026-03-08/
3) Replay events into their Splunk HEC endpoint with resume-token set from manifest; observe duplicate resume-token rejections from HEC and later missing sequence gaps in their reconciliation.

Observed behavior:
- Tenant IDs in exported records appear lowercased (e.g., "fintrak:logincorp") while customer expects original case-preserved strings.
- Manifest contains a "resume_token" that the customer's HEC says was previously used (leading to idempotency rejections).
- Manifest timestamp is present but not RFC3161-signed; customer requires RFC3161 timestamp token and KMS-attested signature evidence.

Expected behavior:
- NDJSON export preserves original tenant ID case exactly as emitted by the control plane.
- Resume tokens in manifest should be monotonic and unique per-delivery; HEC handshake should provide a deterministic resume-token seed and per-bundle nonce to avoid id reuse.
- Provide an RFC3161-signed manifest and corresponding KMS/HSM attestation bundle suitable for regulatory evidence.

Attachments:
- Customer provided sample lines from their reconciliation showing mismatched counts and tenant-id mismatches (attached as customer_recon_excerpt.csv).
- Snippet of S3 manifest they received (manifest.json) and S3 object keys list.

Requested deliverables from Support/Engineering:
- Immediate: Confirm whether case-normalization policy was applied during export and provide a remediation plan for the affected window (2026-03-08).
- Medium: Provide a patch/flag enabling case-preserving tenant IDs for NDJSON exports and a deployed hotfix or backfill plan.
- Evidence: RFC3161-signed manifest for the affected export(s), KMS key id(s) used, public attestation of HSM anchoring, and a signed checksum file for the bundle.
- Operational: A proposed HEC handshake protocol update to include per-bundle nonce to avoid resume-token collisions with downstream idempotency checks.

Customer contact preferences:
- Primary: Compliance lead (email) and weekly sync via Zoom. Customer asked for written evidence before their audit on 2026-03-18.

RFC3161 timestamping is not enabled for this path; can produce on-demand RFC3161 tokens from our HSM but needs a small ops runbook.

That explains case normalization. Patch proposed to respect original tenant_id when case_preserve flag is true. Patch branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-export/pull/452

2026-03-12 — FinTrak Compliance (Customer): Confirm they received interim triage notes. They request expedited RFC3161 manifest and a signed checksum for the bundle for the 2026-03-08 export. They will pause their internal reconciliation until we can provide corrected bundle or clear mapping guidance.

investigation_notes:
Findings summary:
- Export pipeline normalizer contained a compatibility flag that lowercased tenant_id for legacy Splunk customers. This was the likely cause of case mismatch. Query run: SELECT count(*) FROM export_events WHERE tenant_normalized = LOWER(tenant_original) AND export_date = '2026-03-08' returned 1342 rows with normalized tenant values.
- Resume-token reuse: The resume_token in the manifest is constructed as HMAC_SHA256(kms_key, bundle_id || window_start). For repeated replays we discovered bundle_id was derived from a rolling daily counter that resets during a re-run; re-emit jobs reused same bundle_id leading to resume-token collision.
- Signing: Existing manifest uses internal envelope signature; RFC3161 timestamping is available via our HSM but was not integrated into export pipeline.
Hypothesis:
- Combination of lowercasing plus reuse of bundle_id on re-emits caused downstream join failures and HEC idempotency rejections.
Queries/commands used during triage:
- aws s3 ls s3://redwood-exports/fintrak/2026-03-08/ -- recursive
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-exports/fintrak/2026-03-08/manifest.json - | jq .
- SELECT bundle_id, COUNT(*) FROM export_events WHERE export_date = '2026-03-08' GROUP BY bundle_id;
- git blame on exporter normalizer file to identify commit and author (commit 3f7a2b, author: legacy-compat).
next_steps: Backfill: Schedule backfill job to re-emit NDJSON for 2026-03-08 with case_preserve=true. Estimated runtime: 2 hours (job priority: high).
Patch: Merge PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-export/pull/452 after QA in staging and promote to prod behind feature flag.

Evidence bundle: Generate RFC3161 timestamp for manifest(s) from HSM and produce signed checksum file. Deliver to customer via pre-signed S3 link and include KMS key identifiers and attestation. Target delivery: 2026-03-13 18:00 UTC.
HEC handshake: Draft spec v1.1 to include per-bundle nonce and explicit resume-token derivation to avoid collisions; circulate with customer for review.
requested_resolution: Provide re-emitted NDJSON bundle with original tenant-case preserved for 2026-03-08, an RFC3161-signed manifest and signed checksum bundle, and a mitigation plan to prevent resume-token reuse. Confirm completion to customer ahead of audit deadline 2026-03-18.
